_doc: No Law: the script for the voiced lines (#807). The same shape as sheriff_road.json (its _doc and docs/scripts/README.md say the fields). Built lines are copied from config/moments/no_law_murder.json unchanged. Nothing here is approved until Sean taps Script OK. Since 2026-11-17 (#1056): written to the house style, docs/story/DIALOGUE.md. `when` names the StoryState fact a line waits on (the top-level `facts` list says which exist and which gameplay has to add); `was` holds a line's wordings before the rewrite; `added` marks a new line. The murder's and the funeral's lines are in the game (config/moments/no_law_murder.json, funeral.json): a wording here that differs from the game's has status new and is listed for gameplay in docs/scripts/CHANGES.md.
title: No Law
mission: no-law (#773 built the murder; #796 is step 4, the morning after and the sheriff's last day)
status: rewritten 2026-11-17 in the house style (#1056): waiting on Sean's Script OK
sources: config/moments/no_law_murder.json (the built lines, fixed); config/card_game.json (the table's talk, built)
docs/missions/no-law.md (PR #743's branch), #796 and its comments (Cody kills Earl; the red shirt is Kett and isn't in the saloon)
docs/story/OUTLINE.md Act I, VOICES.md (the foreman, Cody, the barkeep, the Baron, the widow, smaller voices), SETUPS.md, WORDS.md (PR #833)
#830: C10 b (the stranger is the Baron's foreman; nobody says so), C12 a, C14 c (roles only)
docs/story/DIALOGUE.md (the house style, #1056); Sean's note on the page (murder.accuse), read 2026-11-17
notes: Harlan doesn't speak: he's sat, unarmed, held (Sean: 'he can't do anything at all').
The sheriff's last day (Beat 5) is No Law's in the game (#796) but its lines are in the sheriff's script (scene 5, day2.*), so his voice is in one place.
The card game's talk at the table (config/card_game.json: 'Ante.', 'Call.', Earl's 'Lady's been kind tonight') is built and belongs on a town-life page later, not here.
Nobody names the red shirt (Kett), says the stranger works for the Baron (K3, K11) or that he shot the sheriff (K14). The foreman's voice is open (s21): written to his built lines, calm and low.
Rewritten 2026-11-17 (#1056). The stranger's, Cody's, Earl's and the barkeep's lines at the table are Sean's or built, and stay word for word.

The stranger's voice (s21), settled for the script: soft-spoken and mannerly, a man who asks leave for what he means to do anyway ('Mind if I sit in a while?'). That courtesy is how the sheriff let him ride up. He says 'ain't' when it suits him.

The town remembers: lines with an 'If:' wait on what you did (packed him, left him, sat at the table, went after Cody, knelt by Earl, what you told the stranger, whether you shook your head at the oath).
The town gets the night wrong in the morning, on purpose: a player who sat at the table knows it.

Sean, 2026-11-17 (decided, #1056): Harlan carries Earl to the doctor's and bangs on the door; the doctor, up with the sheriff, says the man wants burying; Earl lies in the front room till morning. Scenes 'after', 'carry' and 'morning' are written to it. This changes the built murder: Earl is shot and down, not shot dead (gameplay, #1057).

Sean's review, 2026-11-17: the stranger asks Harlan to his own table, buys him a drink, and they talk a minute about the sheriff before Cody comes in. So s26 is simpler: the doctor may say 'Go and get a drink', and whoever walks into the saloon's yard is asked to sit. The oath and 'deputy for now, until the county names a man' are the sheriff's own words: his page, scene 5 (day2.oath, day2.for_now).

setups.what: "Ain't no law left in this valley to save you now."
Cody, the witness (the barman knows him by name; a whole room saw)
Graves: Earl's a recorded death; the sheriff's grave
"Friend", and the bald-faced sorrel (the sheriff's marks; a thing at the rail, not a line)
setups.status: D (Sean 2026-11-13, #906); the sorrel needs a horse coat (art)
the funeral's part P·bible: he stands behind the Baron, silent

setups.what: The outbreak that wasn't (the town already saying 'Utes' on night one)
"That's not the way this works, son." (the widow knows you shook your head)
Harlan's spring: the Baron admires it
Earl carried to the doctor's door; his blood on Harlan's coat; the body in the front room (Sean, 2026-11-17)

cast.name: The stranger (the Baron's foreman)
cast.bible: VOICES.md, The Baron's foreman; s21 open
cast.brief: About fifty, Western, calm and low; friendly the way a man is who can afford it. Few words, never hurried, never raised. Educated or a cowman is Sean's call (s21): the built lines lean educated.

cast.name: Cody
cast.brief: Late twenties, a Texas cowhand gone bad. Loud and short, brave with drink and a crew behind him; a hard flat voice, a sneer in it.

cast.name: Earl
cast.brief: Sixties, a card player, thin and placating; quick to smile, quicker to apologise.

cast.name: The barkeep
cast.brief: Forties, aggrieved and quick, always counting what a thing costs him; a nasal Midwestern voice that rises when he's upset.

cast.name: The drifter
cast.brief: Thirties, a hand between jobs; dry, low, wants no part of anything.

cast.name: The miner at the table
cast.brief: Fifties, a hard-rock man, slow and heavy, a little Cornish (WORDS.md: 'my son' once is enough).

cast.name: A townsman
cast.bible: P·bible (No Law's Beat 1, the town without a sheriff)
cast.brief: Forties, a storekeeper type; worried, talks low, glances over his shoulder.

cast.name: A townswoman
cast.brief: Thirties to forties, plain-spoken, good grammar; brisk, says what she thinks.

cast.name: A bold man in the street
cast.bible: No Law's Beat 1: 'others behave more boldly'
cast.brief: Thirties, a teamster or a hand in town; too loud, a little drunk, enjoying the sheriff's absence.

cast.name: The undertaker
cast.brief: Sixties, unhurried, precise, a dry gallows humour he doesn't know he has.

cast.name: The preacher
cast.brief: Fifties, a Methodist circuit man; carrying voice, plain, unadorned; reads the old words without performing them.

cast.name: The Baron
cast.bible: VOICES.md, The Baron; WORDS.md, The Baron
cast.brief: Sixty, educated, courteous and unhurried; long sentences, never a threat. Eastern or British money: his accent is Sean's call.

cast.name: The sheriff's wife
cast.bible: VOICES.md, The widow (the same voice as in the sheriff's script)
cast.brief: About forty, a Midwestern farm wife with good schooling. Level and low, short; grief held under work.

cast.name: The doctor
cast.bible: VOICES.md, The doctor (the same voice as in the sheriff's script)
cast.brief: Late forties, an educated Easterner; brisk, quiet, dry.

scenes.title: Salt Creek without its sheriff
scenes.setting: The sheriff is at the doctor's. Townsfolk at their evening posts talk about it; some are worried, some bolder for it. Who sends Harlan to the saloon is open (s26): Sean's two ways are written below, both proposed.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: You pass him on Main Street, evening of day 1
lines.delivery: Low, to his neighbour more than to you. The last is how a rumour starts.

words.text: Sheriff's shot. He's at Doc's, and Doc ain't saying.
I'm barring my door tonight.
Road agents, somebody said, or Utes.

lines.speaker: townswoman
lines.trigger: You pass her on Main Street, evening of day 1
lines.delivery: Shaking out a cloth. 'These' with a look at the saloon.

words.text: And her out there with two boys and the stock to see to.
Somebody ought to ride out to her. It won't be any of these men.

lines.speaker: loudmouth
lines.trigger: You pass him by the saloon, evening of day 1
lines.delivery: Too loud, pleased with himself; the street goes quiet round him. A joke tonight. Cody says nearly the same thing over a body.

words.text: Ain't no sheriff tonight, boys!
Who's going to fine me? Doc?

was: No sheriff tonight, boys. Drink where you please.
Who's going to fine me? The doc?

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: He sees you, evening of day 1
lines.delivery: Sizing you up; half thanks, half suspicion.

words.text: You're the one brought him in. From up the creek.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: After town.you
lines.delivery: Wary. He's looking at your hands.

words.text: Doc says that wound was packed proper. Says you done it.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: He sees you, evening of day 1
lines.delivery: Just passing on the news. He doesn't know it was you. You do.

words.text: Freighter found him in the road. Three hours he'd lain there. Somebody must've gone right by him.

lines.speaker: doctor
lines.trigger: Leaving the doctor's that evening (after evening.doctor.go in the sheriff's script)
lines.note: s26: the doctor sends him, if he brought the sheriff in. Sets nolaw.sent_by = doctor.
lines.delivery: At the door, an afterthought. He means it.

words.text: Go and get a drink, Harlan. I would, if I could leave him.

scenes.title: The stranger's table
scenes.when: Night 1, the saloon's yard: the stranger's table, beside the card game
scenes.setting: Sean's review, 2026-11-17: the stranger is sat alone with a bottle; he asks Harlan to sit with him and talk, and buys him a drink. They talk for a minute at most, about the sheriff: about Harlan bringing him in, if he did. The stranger calls the sheriff a good man who didn't deserve it. He is the man who shot him. Then Cody comes in, and the stranger's hand is on Harlan's arm. Harlan is unarmed. (The card game's own talk at Earl's table is built and goes on a town-life page.)

lines.speaker: stranger
lines.trigger: You come into the saloon's yard; he is alone at a table by the card game, and looks up
lines.delivery: Pleasant, unhurried. He already knows your name. He asks leave, as he always does, and pushes the other chair out with his boot.

words.text: Evening. Harlan, isn't it? Sit with me a while, if you've no objection.

was: Evening. Mind if I sit in a while?
lines.note: Sean's review, 2026-11-17: 'he'll ask you to sit with him and talk'. The game has him join you ('Evening. Mind if I sit in a while?'): a change for gameplay.

lines.speaker: stranger
lines.trigger: You sit
lines.delivery: To the barkeep, two fingers up; then to you, a hand flat on the table when you reach for your pocket.

words.text: What'll you take? ... No, put your money up. I asked you.

lines.note: Sean's review, 2026-11-17: 'he buys you a drink'.

lines.speaker: stranger
lines.trigger: The drinks come
lines.when: sheriff.care = good or poor (you brought the sheriff in)
lines.delivery: A man making talk. He is looking at your hands.

words.text: They tell me it was you brought the sheriff in. That's a hard thing to come on, a man lying in the road.

lines.speaker: stranger
lines.trigger: The drinks come, in place of table.talk
lines.delivery: The same easy talk. He doesn't know yet whether you were on that road.

words.text: You'll have heard about the sheriff. Shot on the East Road this morning, not four miles from where we sit.

lines.speaker: stranger
lines.trigger: A swallow later
lines.delivery: Said with his eyes down, turning his glass. Every word of it is true.

words.text: I only met him the once. He seemed a good man. He didn't deserve that.

lines.note: Sean's review, 2026-11-17: 'calls the sheriff a good man and didn't deserve it'. 'The once' was this morning, on the road.

lines.speaker: stranger
lines.trigger: After table.good_man; he waits for your nod or shake
lines.condition: calm, friendly, a little too interested
lines.delivery: Idle. It is the only thing he came to find out. He watches your face.

words.text: He able to talk any, when you got him in?

lines.note: Nod or shake: Harlan can lie to him. Sets nolaw.told_stranger. Not built.

lines.speaker: stranger
lines.trigger: After table.good_man; he waits for your nod or shake
lines.delivery: The same easy talk. He is finding out whether you were on that road.

words.text: You'd have come down that road yourself this morning. ... See anything of it?

lines.speaker: stranger
lines.trigger: You nod
lines.condition: calm; something shuts behind his eyes
lines.delivery: A beat too long. Then he looks at his cards.

words.text: Did he.

lines.speaker: stranger
lines.trigger: You shake your head
lines.delivery: Easy. He believes you, or lets you think so.

words.text: No. I'd not think he could.

lines.speaker: stranger
lines.trigger: You don't answer
lines.delivery: Lets it lie. He has all night.

words.text: No matter.

lines.speaker: stranger
lines.trigger: Cody comes into the yard; the stranger's hand on your arm
lines.delivery: Low, close, not looking at you; the friendliness gone flat.

words.text: Don't move, friend. Whatever happens next, you sit still.

scenes.title: The murder
scenes.setting: Cody walks up, accuses Earl, kicks his chair out from under him and shoots him in the head where he lies. Very quick; not a fair fight. The room goes quiet until the barman.

lines.speaker: cody
lines.trigger: Cody comes into the yard: shouting at Earl from the moment he walks in, before he reaches the table
lines.delivery: Shouted across the yard as he comes, already worked up; the whole room turns. The no-law line comes after, quiet, with Earl on the floor.

words.text: Earl, you cheating son of a bitch!
words.note: Sean's redo, 2026-11-12 (was the built 'Earl. You been dealing off the bottom of that deck.')

lines.speaker: earl
lines.trigger: Right after the accusation
lines.delivery: A nervous smile in it; cut off by the kick.

words.text: Now, Cody, I never...

lines.speaker: cody
lines.trigger: Over Earl on the ground, after the shot
lines.delivery: Not shouted: almost conversational, a man who knows nobody will stop him.

words.text: Ain't no law left in this valley to save you now, Earl.

lines.speaker: barkeep
lines.trigger: The hush after Cody turns away
lines.delivery: Outraged about the wrong thing; the first sound in the room. Sean's punchline: play it straight.

words.text: Jesus, Cody, my chair!

lines.speaker: barkeep
lines.trigger: At Earl's body, ~20 s later
lines.delivery: Starts to give an order and finds there's nobody to give it to.

words.text: Somebody ought to fetch the... hell. Ain't nobody left to fetch.

scenes.title: After
scenes.when: Night 1, the saloon's yard and the street
scenes.setting: Cody walks out; the drifter and the miner leave; the stranger has his word and goes. Earl is down and bleeding, not dead (Sean, 2026-11-17: his wound by the body system). The barkeep tells Harlan to get him to the doctor's. Harlan can follow Cody out instead and see which way he rides. Built: the stranger's lines. New: the rest; the carry is #1057.

lines.speaker: stranger
lines.trigger: Cody's out of the yard; the stranger stands to go
lines.delivery: Friendly again, which is worse; a hand on your shoulder as he passes.

words.text: You didn't see a thing tonight. Nobody did. Remember that.

lines.speaker: stranger
lines.trigger: You point a gun at him
lines.delivery: Unbothered; he's had guns pointed at him before.

words.text: Easy, friend. I ain't the one you want.
Put it up. You'll only get yourself killed.
Walk away. That's my advice.

lines.speaker: drifter
lines.trigger: He gets up to leave (~5 s after Cody's out)
lines.delivery: Picking up his hat and his money. To the table, not to you.

words.text: I'm out.

lines.speaker: miner
lines.trigger: He gets up to leave (~9 s after Cody's out)
lines.delivery: Slow and heavy, looking down at Earl. Fair to him, which makes it worse.

words.text: He were cheating, my son, a dollar at a time, same as ever he did.

lines.speaker: barkeep
lines.trigger: A few seconds after murder.fetch: there's nobody to fetch, so he turns to you
lines.delivery: He has just found there's no sheriff to send for. He picks the nearest man. Part mercy; part that it's his yard.

words.text: He's breathing. Harlan. You. Get him up to Doc's.
Go on! He can't lie there.

lines.note: Sean, 2026-11-17 (#1056, decided): 'who tells Harlan to take him to Doc's': the barkeep, straight after his built 'Ain't nobody left to fetch.'

lines.speaker: barkeep
lines.trigger: You have Earl up and are going out with him
lines.delivery: To your back, and to himself. He means it.

words.text: He owes me four dollars.

lines.speaker: cody
lines.trigger: You follow him out to the street; he's mounting
lines.delivery: Doesn't even look round; then he rides for the foothills.

words.text: Go on back to your cards, farmer.

was: Go on back to your cards, nester.
lines.note: Was 'nester': not in Bartlett (1877), De Vere (1872) or Farmer (1889). 'Farmer' is contempt enough from a cowhand.

scenes.title: Carrying Earl
scenes.when: Night 1, Main Street, the saloon to the doctor's door (#1057, not built)
scenes.setting: Sean, 2026-11-17 (decided): Harlan carries Earl up the street to the doctor's and bangs on the door. The doctor is up with the sheriff. Earl dies on the way by his wound's clock; however fast you are, he is past help. The doctor has him laid in the front room for the night. If you don't carry him (proposed, #1057), he dies where he lies and the saloon's men bring him up in the morning.

lines.speaker: earl
lines.trigger: On the way, a while apart, while he can talk; then nothing
lines.when: nolaw.carried_earl = yes; while his blood loss lets him
lines.delivery: Small, close to your ear. Still trying to smooth it over. Each on its own; the last is a breath.

words.text: Mind my arm.
I left my hat.
Tell Cody I'll make it good. You tell him.
It was only a dollar.

lines.note: Sean, 2026-11-17 (#1056, decided): 'what Earl says on the way if he can talk'. He never says he's dying. The dollar is the miner's (after.miner).

lines.speaker: townswoman
lines.trigger: She sees you pass with him
lines.delivery: From a doorway. She doesn't come out.

words.text: Is that Earl? ... Lord. Doc's got his lamp lit. Go on.

lines.speaker: doctor
lines.trigger: You bang on his door; from inside, before it opens
lines.delivery: Through the door, from the back of the house. He is a long time coming. Bang again and he says the second.

words.text: Who is it? I've a man dying in here.
I hear you! I've only the two hands.

lines.note: Sean, 2026-11-17 (#1056, decided): the doctor is up with the sheriff, and slow to the door.

lines.speaker: doctor
lines.trigger: He opens the door, lamp in hand, and looks at Earl
lines.delivery: One look, a thumb to the man's eye. No drama. He has been losing a man all day.

words.text: This man wants burying, Harlan, not doctoring.

lines.note: Sean, 2026-11-17 (#1056, decided): 'He needs a grave, not a doctor.' His sense, in the doctor's mouth ('wants' for needs).

lines.speaker: doctor
lines.trigger: A beat after
lines.when: sheriff.care = good or poor (you brought the sheriff here this morning)
lines.delivery: Counting, as he does.

words.text: That's two you've carried to this door today.

lines.speaker: doctor
lines.trigger: A beat after, in place of carry.two
lines.when: sheriff.care = left (you left the sheriff on the road)
lines.delivery: He knows a freighter brought the other. He looks at you, not at Earl.

words.text: This one you carried.

lines.speaker: doctor
lines.trigger: Then
lines.delivery: Already turning back to the stairs.

words.text: Lay him in the front room. On the table. There's a sheet on the chair.
Then go home. I've the sheriff to sit with.

scenes.title: The morning after
scenes.when: Day 2, morning, Main Street and the doctor's front room (#796; the body at the doctor's is #1057)
scenes.setting: The town wakes to the news and tells the night wrong. Earl lies under a sheet in the doctor's front room (Sean, 2026-11-17), where Harlan passes him on the way in to the sheriff; the undertaker comes for him there. Nobody arrests Cody. Then someone sends for Harlan: the sheriff is dying.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: You pass him on day 2
lines.delivery: Each teller surer than the last, and each wrong a different way. Only the first is true.

words.text: Cody said there weren't no law to stop him, or some such.
Earl went for a knife, the way I heard it.
Two of them done it. One held him.
Cody give him a fair chance. That's what Cody's friends say.

lines.speaker: townswoman
lines.trigger: You pass her on day 2
lines.delivery: Disapproving of the whole saloon and everyone in it.

words.text: A dozen men sat and watched it done.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: He sees you on day 2
lines.delivery: Not loud; he wants an answer and doesn't expect one.

words.text: They say you sat at that very table. Sat right through it.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: He sees you on day 2, in place of morning.you_were_there
lines.delivery: Looking at your coat. He doesn't know what to make of you.

words.text: They say you carried him clear up the street. ... That his blood on you?

lines.speaker: townswoman
lines.trigger: She passes you on day 2
lines.delivery: Not unkind. It is the nearest anybody comes to thanking you.

words.text: Cold water, Mr. Harlan, not hot. Hot sets it.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: He sees you on day 2
lines.delivery: Not unkind. He thinks it was a fool thing and half admires it.

words.text: Somebody saw you go out after him. On foot. After a man on a horse.

lines.speaker: loudmouth
lines.trigger: You pass him on day 2
lines.delivery: Last night's man, sober. He heard his own joke come out of Cody's mouth.

words.text: I said who's going to fine me. Hell. I was only funning.
He'll be back. Why wouldn't he?

lines.speaker: undertaker
lines.trigger: In the doctor's front room, measuring Earl under the sheet (if you didn't carry him: at the saloon's yard)
lines.delivery: Writing in his book as he talks; reads the entry back. He is only being exact.

words.text: Earl. Nobody can give me his other name. Shot by one Cody, before witnesses. Pine box, charged to the county.
He had on him a deck of cards, a pocket knife and sixty cents.
The saloon wants four dollars and a chair set down against that.

lines.speaker: doctor
lines.trigger: You stop by the sheet in his front room, on the way in to the sheriff
lines.delivery: In passing, rolling his sleeves down. He has been up all night with the other one.

words.text: He was dead when you knocked. I'd not have you think it was the door.

lines.note: Sean, 2026-11-17 (#1056, decided): 'the doctor who didn't open, or opened too late'. He tells you it wasn't the wait, which is how you know he has thought about it.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: He finds you on day 2 (the doctor sent him)
lines.delivery: Out of breath from looking for you.

words.text: Harlan! Doc's asking for you. Says the sheriff's sinking.

lines.note: Then the sheriff's last day: the sheriff's script, scene 5 (day2.*)

scenes.title: The funeral
scenes.when: Day 2 or 3, the cemetery on the hill (Beat 6, not built)
scenes.setting: Quiet, not a set piece. The town gathers; hats come off. The Baron offers the widow a price for her claim at the graveside, the foreman behind him saying nothing (S39). Harlan can attend, watch from a distance or miss it.

lines.speaker: preacher
lines.trigger: The service at the grave
lines.delivery: The old burial words, read plainly into the wind; no performance.

words.text: Man that is born of a woman hath but a short time to live, and is full of misery. He cometh up, and is cut down, like a flower.
words.note: the Book of Common Prayer's burial service (1662), public domain

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: Among the mourners, after
lines.delivery: Hat in his hands; a small true thing about the dead man.

words.text: He fined me twice, and I'll own I had it coming both times.

was: He'd come in Saturdays. One drink. Never two.

lines.speaker: barkeep
lines.trigger: Among the mourners, after (the game's town_2)
lines.delivery: It still bothers him.

words.text: Never once took a drink on the house. I'd pour it and he'd leave the dime.

lines.speaker: baron
lines.trigger: At the graveside, after the service, to the widow; you're near enough to hear
lines.delivery: Hat in hand, voice lowered, perfectly kind, and long. Nothing in it you could object to.

words.text: It is a hard day, ma'am, and I'd not trouble you on it, only to say that when that place grows too much for you, as it may, I hope you will come to me before another. You'll not find a fairer figure.

was: A hard day, ma'am. When that place grows too much for you, come to me first. You'll not find a fairer figure.

lines.speaker: widow
lines.trigger: Her answer to the Baron
lines.delivery: Not raised. She doesn't look at him. It is all the answer he gets.

words.text: He's not covered over yet.

lines.speaker: baron
lines.trigger: After her answer
lines.delivery: A small bow. Nothing in it but manners, and no doubt at all that the other day will come.

words.text: Forgive me, ma'am; it was ill-timed of me, and we will speak of it another day.

lines.speaker: baron
lines.trigger: He passes you on his way out
lines.delivery: Already knows your name; lets you see that he does.

words.text: Mr. Harlan. A sad day for the county, and I'd not have chosen it to make your acquaintance.

was: Mr. Harlan. A sad day for the county.

lines.speaker: baron
lines.trigger: He passes you on his way out, in place of funeral.baron_you
lines.delivery: Praise, from the man who had it done. He lets you see he knows everything about that morning.

words.text: Mr. Harlan, they tell me he had a night with his wife that he'd not have had but for you, and I call that well done.

lines.speaker: baron
lines.trigger: A step later, half turned back
lines.delivery: An afterthought, the way a man admires a horse he hasn't bid on yet.

words.text: You have the spring above the creek, I'm told, and the only sweet water for some miles. I have admired it from the road.

lines.note: Plants the Baron's want where the player is the one wanted from (SETUPS M6: Harlan's spring).

lines.speaker: stranger
lines.trigger: He follows the Baron out, past you
lines.delivery: Two fingers to his hat brim and the same easy smile as last night. One word.

words.text: Good morning to you, Deputy.

lines.note: The man from the table, behind the Baron. If the sorrel is at the Baron's buggy (art), the player has all three marks.

lines.speaker: widow
lines.trigger: As the mourners go
lines.when: nolaw.funeral = attended and sheriff.care = good or poor
lines.delivery: Brief; she has a hundred hands to shake.

words.text: You came, Mr. Harlan. He'd have noticed that.

lines.speaker: widow
lines.trigger: As the mourners go, in place of funeral.you_came
lines.delivery: Dry. Not a smile. She leaves it there.

words.text: He told me you shook your head at him. It tickled him.

lines.speaker: widow
lines.trigger: As the mourners go, in place of funeral.you_came
lines.delivery: She looks at you a moment and gives you your name. Nothing else.

words.text: Mr. Harlan.
